subject: Spend thresholds & smoothing: hosted API commit options and grace periods
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@atlasai.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: Question on spend thresholds and smoothing for hosted API

Hi Olga,

We're evaluating Redwood for production inference (hosted API) and have a few questions about minimum monthly spend and how you handle usage volatility. A couple specifics:

- Do you require a minimum monthly commit for hosted customers who don't take Dedicated yet? If so, what are typical entry bands and flexibility for startups? 
- Can commit volumes be smoothed (e.g., 60-day rolling average) or do overages get billed immediately? Any grace periods for first few months? 
- Is there a way to have a temporary lower commit for Q1 with an automatic step-up once we hit traction? 
- What are the per-token list rates and typical discount bands for 1M/10M/100M tokens? 

We're a Series B company; likely initial monthly spend is lumpy while we ramp. Would appreciate a ballpark response we can share with our CFO/procurement.

Thanks,
Sophie Turner
Head of Product
AtlasAI

Attachments: none

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Fwd: Question on spend thresholds and smoothing for hosted API

Folks — Sophie from AtlasAI (Series B) asked about minimum monthly commit and smoothing. We should propose something startup-friendly but protect economics. Draft proposal below; please flag risks.

Draft proposal bullets:
- Offer three starter bands for Hosted API (no Dedicated):
  1) Startup Band: $5k/month minimum, 30% discount off list, 60-day rolling smoothing for overages in first 3 months, and $10k onboarding credit applied to first 2 invoices.
  2) Growth Band: $25k/month minimum, 40% discount, 45-day smoothing, flexible quarter-to-quarter step-up with 30-day notice.
  3) Scale Band: $100k/month minimum, 50% discount, 30-day smoothing, commitment term 12 months.
- Overage treatment: prorated overage billed monthly; for Startup Band allow 2-month grace in first quarter where overage exposure is capped at 25% of commit and any excess converted to true-up credit.
- Early reduction/rollback: allow one downward adjustment after 90 days with 60-day notice and a pro-rated termination/adjustment fee equal to 10% of remaining quarter commit.
- Ratecard (gen tokens): list $14 / 1M tokens; effective price after discounts.

I've attached a provisional ratecard spreadsheet. Please review and suggest alternate thresholds if you think $5k is too low.

- Olga

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@atlasai.com>, procurement@atlasai.com
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Question on spend thresholds and smoothing for hosted API

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear questions. Following internal alignment, here's a concise set of options tailored for AtlasAI's profile:

1) Startup Band (recommended for Series B ramp):
   - $5,000/month minimum commit
   - 30% discount off list rates
   - 60-day rolling smoothing for billing; first 3 months include a two-month grace where overage exposure is capped at 25% of commit
   - $10,000 onboarding credit applied across first two invoices
   - One-time SOW; 6-month minimum term with option to convert to Growth Band

2) Growth Band:
   - $25,000/month minimum
   - 40% discount
   - 45-day smoothing window
   - Quarter-to-quarter step-up with 30 days' notice (no penalty)

3) Scale Band:
   - $100,000/month minimum
   - 50% discount
   - 30-day smoothing
   - 12-month commitment; standard termination provisions

Per-token list rate (generation): $14 / 1M tokens. Embeddings and special model rates vary; see attached provisional-ratecard-ATLAS-v1.xlsx. We can provide a short billing appendix that codifies smoothing windows and the initial grace period.

If this looks reasonable I can spin up a draft SOW and send for signature (DocuSign). If procurement prefers alternative protections (e.g., capped overage liability) let us know and we'll review.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Mid-Market Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: provisional-ratecard-ATLAS-v1.xlsx, SOW-draft-Atlas-v1.docx

If you can send the SOW with those two small edits I'll run it with procurement today. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Thanks,
Sophie
